reason: This text is the Song of Moses (Exodus 15), in which the Hebrews/Israelites explicitly sing praises to Yahweh following their deliverance at the Red Sea. The passage demonstrates devotion to Yahweh as foundational to Hebrew identity: they declare 'I will sing to the Lord' (אָשִׁירָה לַיהוָה), identify 'This is my God' (זֶה אֱלִי), recognize Yahweh as their source of salvation and protection, acknowledge Him as a warrior who fights for them, and proclaim His eternal reign ('The Lord will reign forever and ever'). The entire composition centers on Yahweh as the supreme power and object of worship, with no mention of alternative allegiances. This represents the Hebrews understanding themselves as followers of Yahweh in the most fundamental theological sense.
